short: Cu clusters immobilized on Cd-defective cadmium sulfide nano
title: Cu clusters immobilized on Cd-defective cadmium sulfide nano-rods towards photocatalytic CO2 reduction

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Edge Cd vacancies of CdS nanorods can trap ultrasmall Cu clusters that act as active sites for CO2 photoreduction. CdS nanorods (CR) as the host photocatalyst.
states.detail: Absorbed: h1 (HYP/hypothesis), d1 (DES/base_system), d2 (DES/modification), p1 (PRC/synthesis), p2 (PRC/treatment), p3 (PRC/synthesis)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Cd atoms are missing along the CdS nanorod edge (Cd vacancies). An ultrasmall Cu cluster, a few nm across (~1.2-1.9 x 3.6 nm), sits at the vacancy-bearing nanorod edge.
states.detail: Absorbed: s1 (STR/defect/point), s2 (STR/microstructure/feature_size), s3 (STR/chemistry/composition), s4 (STR/interface). Premises: Cu K-edge shoulders 8980.9, 8982.1, 8986.4 eV mark Cu0, Cu+ and Cu2+ [14]; Cu-S bonding gives a wavelet-transform maximum near 4.9 A-1 [42]

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Photogenerated electrons move from CdS to the Cu clusters, improving electron-hole separation. CuCR SCC binds CO2 more strongly than CR at low coverage (Qst ~25 vs ~9 kJ/mol).
states.detail: Absorbed: r1 (PRP/descriptor), r2 (PRP/value), m1 (MEC/pathway), r3 (PRP/value). Premises: EPR g = 2.08 is the Cu2+ signal [41,47]; Cu 3d orbitals hybridise with CO2 2p orbitals, strengthening CO2 chemisorption [54]

states.title: Performance state
states.head: CuCR SCC yields ~38 umol/g CO in 5 h (~7.7 umol/g/h), about twice CR and CR-H

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Cu clusters anchored in edge Cd vacancies of CdS nanorods double CO photoproduction and raise CO selectivity via interfacial charge transfer and CO2 activation
